description: Read a merchant's public record by merchant_id: owner address, metadata URI, merchant rank, active/suspended flags, registration time, the merchant-authored description and landing page URL, and the ids of its listed products. tos_status (accepted, grace, required, owner_changed, not_published) and tos_can_trade say whether the merchant has accepted the Merchant Terms of Service; one that cannot trade gets no ref links and no x402 payments once its chain's gate is on, and tos_next names the fix. tos_upcoming_version and tos_sign_by announce a new version to accept before that date. merchant_id IS the merchant's ERC-8004 agent id — MerchantRegistry mints no ids of its own — and id 0 is a real merchant. Unauthenticated: this returns only what GET /v1/merchant/:id already publishes. A merchant that is inactive or suspended reads as not-found, exactly as it does over REST; the on-chain flag is the authoritative view of a merchant's own state and activate_merchant (opensouk-signer) reports it. Ranks are relative, not absolute: compare with platform_mean. reputation is the platform's reading (merchants/products: exceptional / strong / solid / mixed / weak / new; reviewers: highly_respected / credible / steady / unsteady / poor_record / newcomer); transferred=true means the agent identity changed owner — its reputation was earned before the transfer and its reviews are excluded from review lists and product totals; new / newcomer means too little data, not a low score; null means too few peers to compare. Product rank weights each review by its author's Review Rank, so it can lag what reviews say — read avg_rating and rating_count alongside it.

chain_id.description: EVM chain id; omit for Base

merchant_id.description: Merchant on-chain NFT id (equals its ERC-8004 agent id)

name: get_merchant
